stages.name: Production possibility frontiers
stages.title: Production possibility frontiers
stages.sub: After this, the student can read a PPF diagram for opportunity cost, growth, decline and efficiency.

steps.q: An economy only makes two things: tractors and bicycles. To keep the model simple, economists assume nothing else about the economy changes while they study this. What are they using?
steps.right: A simplified model holding other things constant
steps.wrong: A full record of the real economy
steps.hint: Think about how economists usually study one relationship at a time.
steps.pre: So they build a simple two-good model, using

steps.q: With fixed land, workers and machines, the economy can make lots of combinations of tractors and bicycles, but not unlimited amounts of both. What does a line showing every combination it can just about achieve represent?
steps.right: The maximum it can produce with its current resources
steps.wrong: The amount it currently chooses to produce
steps.hint: Think about the biggest combinations possible, not what is actually being made today.

steps.q: To draw this boundary, you need to know the most tractors possible with zero bicycles, the most bicycles possible with zero tractors, and the combinations in between. What are you doing when you plot all of these points and join them?
steps.wrong: Choosing which point the economy should pick
steps.hint: Is this about building the diagram, or about picking one point on it?

steps.q: The economy is at a point on the frontier making many tractors and few bicycles. It moves along the frontier to make one more bicycle. Since it is already at the maximum, what must happen to tractors?
steps.right: Some tractors must be given up
steps.hint: It is already on the boundary, so getting more of one good only comes from having less of the other.

steps.right: No, it could produce more of both goods
steps.wrong: Yes, it is already at its maximum
